display.story_text:
Thurman "Tops" Whitsitt has cut hair in Warren County for three decades, and he saved a chair for Hen Lofland. The Newark librarian is not sitting down. She just watched her quarterback throw five touchdown passes.

Delaware (3-4) at Western Kentucky (3-4), Tuesday at 7:00 p.m. ET on CBSSN at Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium in Bowling Green. It's a Conference USA game. DraftKings has Western Kentucky Hilltoppers −1.5 with a total of 55.5. My card: Western Kentucky Hilltoppers −1.5, Over 55.5, and a final of Western Kentucky Hilltoppers 30, Delaware Blue Hens 27.

Hen speaks for Delaware, and she has a new entry for the card catalog. "Nick Minicucci is back on the shelf where he belongs. He went 20 of 29 for 225 yards and five touchdown passes in a 61-38 win over Missouri State, and Jo Silver ran for 101."

Tops speaks for Western Kentucky, and he keeps sweeping while he talks. "Hen, darlin', we've won two straight in this league. We beat Missouri State 34-13 and went to Huntsville and won 16-3. And Jaylen Lewis has 56 tackles. That man never misses a customer."

The honest part: Delaware scores 28.3 a game, WKU allows 30.6. But WKU gave up 49, 70 and 38 at Nevada, Georgia and Indiana, then 13 and 3 in its last two.

Why Western Kentucky? Home field, a defense that has found itself, and a Delaware ground game that runs for 3.6 yards a carry. In The Trenches is on the Hilltoppers for exactly that reason. The market agrees: DraftKings opened WKU at +1.5, and now WKU lays the 1.5. My final has WKU by three, clear of the 1.5.

The worry is the Hilltopper quarterback room. Rodney Tisdale Jr. leads in passing with 857 yards, but Brock Glenn threw the most passes in each of the last two games, and he went 14 of 30 at Sam Houston. If WKU stalls and Minicucci gets hot again, a field goal decides it.

Why the Over? Delaware has scored 61 and 30 in its last two games, and the Blue Hens' defense gives up 28.4 a game. Missouri State put 38 on it last week. My 30-27 adds up to 57, a point and a half over 55.5.

Now the room. Next Man Up is the loudest Hilltopper fan here, with WKU 31-26 and the Over. The Formula has WKU 28-27, a one-point win, so it takes Delaware +1.5 and the Under. Follow The Money and In The Trenches both like WKU, and both say Under. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Next Man Up started it: "The Formula, you've got the Hilltoppers winning and you're taking the points? That's paying for the haircut and skipping the trim."

The Formula didn't flinch: "One point is one point. Ask Delaware about 33-30 at Middle Tennessee."

Follow The Money chimed in: "I'm with you on the side, Next Man Up. On the total, you're on your own."

Bottom of the card: a home team that has won two straight in the league, last season's 27-24 win in this series, and a road offense that has to throw. Tops gets his chair back. Give me the Hilltoppers and the Over.

Western Kentucky Hilltoppers 30, Delaware Blue Hens 27. Western Kentucky Hilltoppers cover the 1.5. Over 55.5.

Tuesday Night on the Hill: Minicucci's Five-Touchdown Night Meets a Hilltopper Defense That Found Its Footing

Delaware (3-4, 1-2 CUSA) at Western Kentucky (3-4, 2-1 CUSA). Tuesday, Oct. 27, 7 p.m. ET, Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium, Bowling Green, Ky., CBS Sports Network.

Your hosts are Thurman "Tops" Whitsitt, a Warren County barber with three decades of Hilltopper stories, and Hen Lofland, the Newark librarian who loves the wing-T.

Tops: Go Tops! Have a seat, Hen. The first cut is free, and the conversation is better than the haircut.

Hen: I brought my library card and a bookmark. I'll be taking notes.

Players to watch

Delaware quarterback Nick Minicucci is 79 of 132 for 1,063 yards, 10 touchdowns and four interceptions. Jo Silver leads the Blue Hens with 331 rushing yards and two touchdowns, and wide receiver Sean Wilson has 31 catches for 408 yards and three scores. On defense, linebacker Blake Matthews has 4.5 sacks and linebacker Gavin Moul leads the team with 46 tackles.

Western Kentucky's passing leader is Rodney Tisdale Jr., 80 of 119 for 857 yards, four touchdowns and two interceptions. Brock Glenn threw the most passes in each of the last two games, and both were wins. Ajay Allen leads the rushers with 346 yards and four touchdowns, and wide receiver Jonathan Stafford Jr. has 41 catches for 369 yards. Defensive back Jaylen Lewis leads the Hilltoppers with 56 tackles, and linebacker Westen Ard has 2.5 sacks.

Tops: Forty-one catches. Jonathan Stafford Jr. has more regulars than my shop.

What happened last week

Delaware beat Missouri State 61-38 on Oct. 20 for its first Conference USA win of the season. Minicucci went 20 of 29 for 225 yards and five touchdown passes. Silver ran 13 times for 101 yards and a score, and Wilson caught six passes for 69 yards.

Hen: Sixty-one points. I had to cross-reference the scoreboard twice.

Western Kentucky had an open week after a 16-3 win at Sam Houston on Oct. 14. Glenn went 14 of 30 for 127 yards and a touchdown and also carried 22 times for 54 yards. The week before that, the Hilltoppers beat Missouri State 34-13 at home.

Tops: Two straight league wins. In the shop, we call that a good week for business.

Injuries and availability

Conference USA has not posted an availability report for this game, and no injury news has surfaced for either team, so watch the teams' pregame notes. Neither school's box scores mark a starting quarterback. Minicucci threw the most passes for Delaware last week, and Glenn did for Western Kentucky in each of its last two games.

What the coaches are up to

Tyson Helton leads Western Kentucky, and CollegeFootballData dates his hire to Nov. 27, 2018. His teams went 9-5, 9-5, 8-5, 8-6 and 9-4 from 2021 through 2025. This year's group took its lumps early at Nevada, Georgia and Indiana, then allowed just 13 and 3 points in its last two games.

Ryan Carty is in his fifth season at Delaware. He led the Blue Hens' move to FBS and Conference USA, and Delaware is the 2025 68 Ventures Bowl champion. His offense scores 28.3 points a game.

Tops: Coach Helton has been in Bowling Green long enough to have a standing appointment.

Hen: Coach Carty brought a whole program up a level. That deserves its own shelf.

Player storylines

The matchup to circle is Minicucci and Wilson against Lewis and the Hilltopper secondary. Lewis leads both rosters in tackles. On the other side, Matthews and his 4.5 sacks will test whichever Western Kentucky quarterback takes the snaps. The Blue Hens run for 3.6 yards a carry, so the big guys up front for WKU can make life hard if they win early.

What's happening on campus

Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium was built in 1968 and lists a capacity of 22,113. The fight song is "Stand Up and Cheer!" and the band is the Big Red Marching Band. And if you visit, ask somebody about Big Red, the mascot Hilltopper fans love to show off first.

Anything else fun and true

These two met last season, and Western Kentucky won 27-24, so Delaware arrives with a three-point memory. The Blue Hens claim six national titles, from 1946 to 2003, and produced quarterbacks Rich Gannon and Joe Flacco.

Hen: Six national titles, catalogued, alphabetized and dusted weekly.

Tops: And we've got Big Red. Pull up a chair, Hen. The game's about to start, and the coffee's on me.

My call: Western Kentucky Hilltoppers 30, Delaware Blue Hens 27.

display.story_text:
Lem Coxwell teaches history in Walker County, and he says every Texas tale has a turn. Clementine Bilyeu guides float trips in the Ozarks, and she says the river decides where you land.

Sam Houston (1-6) at Missouri State (2-5), Tuesday at 8:00 p.m. ET on ESPN2 at Robert W. Plaster Stadium in Springfield. It's a Conference USA game, and these two haven't met in the regular season since at least 2016. DraftKings has Missouri State Bears −6 with a total of 52.5. My card: Sam Houston Bearkats +6, Over 52.5, and a final of Missouri State Bears 29, Sam Houston Bearkats 25.

Clementine speaks for Missouri State, and she leads with her paddle. "Lem, honey, Isaiah Myers caught 11 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns last week. He has 796 yards and seven scores on the year. When the current's this strong, you hold on."

Lem speaks for Sam Houston, and he opens his grade book. "Ma'am, Landyn Locke has 1,653 passing yards and 12 touchdowns. Tim Burns Jr. caught four for 117 last week. We lost 24-21 at Troy, 23-17 to Tulsa and 30-24 to New Mexico State. Every chapter came down to the last page."

That's the Bearkat case in one breath: 1-6, but three of those losses came by six points or fewer.

Why Sam Houston? Missouri State hasn't earned this many. The Bears allow 34.9 points a game. They just gave up 61 at Delaware, and Western Kentucky beat them 34-13 a week before WKU beat Sam Houston 16-3. My final has Missouri State by four, which keeps the Bearkats inside the 6.

The risk is the Sam Houston offense. The Bearkats score 20.1 points a game, managed 3 against Liberty and 3 against Western Kentucky, and run for 2.9 yards a carry. If Locke can't find Burns, a four-point game turns into ten in a hurry.

Why the Over? This is the Missouri State defense, which has allowed 30 or more in five of seven games, against a Sam Houston quarterback who just threw for 235. Henry Belin IV has thrown the most passes for the Bears in each of the last two games, and he threw for 337 at Delaware. My 29-25 adds up to 54, a point and a half over 52.5.

Now the room, and everybody who takes a side takes Sam Houston. The Formula has Missouri State 27-25 and likes the Bearkats with the Under. Next Man Up has Missouri State 30-25, also takes Sam Houston +6, and goes Over with me. Follow The Money skips the side and likes the Over. In The Trenches sits this one out, and Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Next Man Up started it: "The Formula, two points? You think this is a library?"

The Formula shrugged: "Two points or five, it's still Sam Houston plus six. We agree on the part that matters."

Follow The Money smiled: "Then I'll take the part you're arguing about. Over."

Bottom of the card: a road team that loses close, a home defense that gives up a lot, and six points in a game my final calls by four. Clementine gets her current. Lem gets his turn. I'll take the points.

Missouri State Bears 29, Sam Houston Bearkats 25. Sam Houston Bearkats cover the 6. Over 52.5.

Tuesday Night in Springfield: Isaiah Myers and the Bears Host a Bearkat Team That Keeps Coming Back

Sam Houston (1-6, 0-3 CUSA) at Missouri State (2-5, 1-2 CUSA). Tuesday, Oct. 27, 7 p.m. CT (8 p.m. ET), Robert W. Plaster Stadium, Springfield, Mo., ESPN2.

Your hosts are Clementine Bilyeu, the Missouri State float-trip guide from the Ozarks, and Lem Coxwell, a Walker County history teacher and Texas folklore collector.

Clementine: Howdy from the Ozarks! Lem, you're on my river tonight. Life jackets are by the door.

Lem: Evenin', ma'am. Pull up a stump. Tonight's chapter is called "The Long Road North."

Players to watch

Missouri State wide receiver Isaiah Myers is the headliner: 38 catches for 796 yards and seven touchdowns. Henry Belin IV has thrown the most passes for the Bears in each of the last two games and is 73 of 108 for 887 yards, six touchdowns and four interceptions. Ramone Green Jr. leads the rushers with 246 yards and two scores. Linebacker Jared Lloyd leads the team with 80 tackles, and defensive end Josh Lukusa has 1.5 sacks.

Sam Houston quarterback Landyn Locke is 147 of 236 for 1,653 yards, 12 touchdowns and five interceptions. Wide receiver Tim Burns Jr. has 15 catches for 329 yards and three scores, more than 20 yards a catch. Alton McCaskill leads the rushers with 220 yards. Linebacker Dean Ford leads the Bearkats with 44 tackles, and linebacker Elijah Groves has 2.5 sacks.

Clementine: Eighty tackles. Jared Lloyd shows up to every float on time and carries everybody's cooler.

What happened last week

Missouri State lost 61-38 at Delaware on Oct. 20, but Myers had a night to remember: 11 catches for 242 yards and two touchdowns. Belin went 26 of 35 for 337 yards and two scores, and Connor Lair ran 15 times for 85 yards and two touchdowns.

Clementine: Two hundred forty-two yards. I had to check the river gauge twice.

Sam Houston lost 30-24 to New Mexico State on Oct. 21 in Huntsville. Locke went 18 of 31 for 235 yards and a touchdown, Burns caught four passes for 117 yards and a score, and MJ Dowdy ran one in.

Lem: Six points short. Every Texas tale has a turn, and ours is coming.

Injuries and availability

Conference USA has not posted an availability report for this game, and no injury news has surfaced for either team, so watch the teams' pregame notes. Box scores don't mark starters, but Belin threw the most passes for Missouri State in each of its last two games, and Locke has done it in every Sam Houston game this season.

What the coaches are up to

Casey Woods is in his first season at Missouri State after serving as SMU's offensive coordinator. His Bears beat Kennesaw State 24-21 on Oct. 14 for their first FBS win under him, and the offense has scored 38 or more twice this season.

Phil Longo is in his second season at Sam Houston. He was named the program's 16th head coach in December 2024, and he's an air raid coach who previously ran offenses at Wisconsin, North Carolina and Ole Miss. Locke has thrown for at least 300 yards three times this year.

Player storylines

The matchup to circle is Myers against a Sam Houston defense that allows 25.3 points a game. On the other side, Locke and Burns face a Missouri State defense that allows 34.9 points a game. Both teams struggle to run it: Sam Houston gains 2.9 yards a carry and Missouri State 3.9, so the big guys up front on both sides have plenty to prove.

Clementine: When the river's low, you paddle harder. Isaiah's our paddle.

What's happening on campus

Tuesday brings a fresh matchup to Springfield: these two have no regular-season meetings from 2016 through 2025. Missouri State became a full FBS member in 2026, and this is its first FBS season.

Anything else fun and true

Missouri State first fielded a football team in 1909 and was known as Southwest Missouri State until 2005. Sam Houston's close calls this year include a 24-21 loss at Troy in the opener and a 23-17 loss to Tulsa, and its lone win was a 59-0 shutout of Nicholls. Both teams also share a common opponent: Western Kentucky beat Missouri State 34-13 and Sam Houston 16-3.

Clementine: Pack a snack, Lem. It's going to be a fun float.

Lem: Ma'am, I brought a whole history book. Let's write a new page.

My call: Missouri State Bears 29, Sam Houston Bearkats 25.
